channel.title: GeoPulse. Geopolitics in brief
channel.description: Signal-first briefings on geopolitics, edited by Lavkesh Dwivedi.

item.title: Iran offers new proposal amid stalled US peace talks
item.description: Iran handed a new proposal to Pakistan on Thursday evening, according to Iranian state media, amid stalled US peace talks. The text of the proposal was handed to mediator Pakistan on Thursday (Apr 30) evening, Iranian state media reported.

item.title: As Israel Entrenches, Frustration With Hezbollah Turns to Support
item.description: In Lebanon, frustration with Hezbollah is turning to support as Israel's actions in the south escalate. Many are seeking protection from the group amid the fraying cease-fire. With the cease-fire fraying and Israel demolishing villages in the south, many Hezbollah supporters in Lebanon are putting aside their annoyance with the group and turning to it for protection.

item.title: Thompson-Herah happy to be back in competition after missing Paris due to injury
item.description: Thompson-Herah returned to competition after missing Paris due to injury. Thompson-Herah happy to be back in competition after missing Paris due to injury.

item.title: Iran has sent latest proposal to U.S. via Pakistan, state media reports
item.description: The UAE expressed distrust in Iran over Hormuz, hindering peace efforts. The Trump administration previously stated its war in Iran had been 'terminated' before a 60-day deadline. Trump administration says its war in Iran has been ’terminated’ before 60-day deadline.

item.title: In Bulgaria, a New Government Challenges an Old Puppet Master
item.description: Bulgaria's new government aims to reduce Delyan Peevski's hold on power. Delyan Peevski was a focus of protests that led to Bulgarian elections. Can a new government shake his hold on power?

item.title: Strain on food, fuel and aid systems continues
item.description: The Middle East crisis strains global food, fuel, and aid systems. The strain on food, fuel and aid systems worldwide continues as the the Middle East crisis deepens. Rising oil prices, supply disruptions and mounting transport costs are affecting humanitarian operations and access to essential goods far beyond the region.

item.title: What the End of Saudi Arabia’s Big-Spending Era Means for the Kingdom and Beyond
item.description: Saudi Arabia is pulling back from a costly golf venture due to financial concerns. The kingdom is pulling back from a costly and high-profile golf venture amid mounting financial concerns, raising questions about its plans.

item.title: Pentagon reaches agreements with leading AI companies
item.description: The Pentagon reached agreements with leading AI companies, including Google and Microsoft, to develop and deploy AI technologies for military use. The agreements aim to accelerate AI adoption in the US military.

item.title: Vivian Balakrishnan to meet Gulf leaders on working visit to Middle East
item.description: Singapore's foreign minister, Vivian Balakrishnan, will visit the UAE, Oman, Saudi Arabia, and Qatar from May 2 to May 5. His working visit is expected to strengthen ties with Gulf leaders.

item.title: 'Treacherous Aggression': UAE Says Iran Cannot Be Trusted Over Hormuz
item.description: The UAE has expressed distrust towards Iran over the Strait of Hormuz, calling its actions "treacherous aggression." The Iranian blockade has largely closed the strategic waterway. Strait Of Hormuz remains largely closed because of an Iranian blockade.

item.title: Chinese Court Rules AI Automation Is Not Valid Reason For Firing Employees
item.description: A Chinese court ruled that AI automation is not a valid reason for firing employees. The decision aims to protect workers from unfair dismissal due to technological changes. Chinese court states AI automation is not a major reason for employee dismissal.

item.title: Hegseth says clock paused on deadline to seek approval for Iran war
item.description: US Defence Secretary Hegseth announced that the deadline for seeking approval for Iran war has been paused. The ceasefire will stop the clock for the president to report to Congress.

item.title: Uganda copying Russia and China with new bill designed to crush dissent, say critics
item.description: Uganda proposes a law with up to 20 years in prison for promoting foreign interests and restricts overseas-funded groups.

item.title: Is Myanmar's military winning the civil war?
item.description: Myanmar's military is stemming losses and reclaiming territory after five years of war with armed resistance groups. After five years of war, armed resistance groups still challenge Myanmar's military across much of the country.

item.title: Antigua and Barbuda prime minister set to win fourth term in election
item.description: Gaston Browne is set to win a fourth term as Antigua and Barbuda's prime minister with 15 of 17 seats.

item.title: Riots erupt over Australian Aboriginal girl’s murder as suspect arrested
item.description: Riots erupted in Australia after a suspect was arrested for the murder of five-year-old Kumanjayi Little Baby. Australian authorities appeal for calm after riots over killing of five-year-old Kumanjayi Little Baby.

item.title: Fertiliser crisis caused by Iran war sparks global food security fears
item.description: The Iran war sparked a fertiliser crisis, causing global food security fears due to shortages and supply chain issues. Fertiliser crisis caused by Iran war sparks global food security fears Euronews. com.

item.title: Iran war expands press crackdown, leaving information vacuum
item.description: Iran tightened press controls, treating truth as a security threat, and strictly controlling information. For many journalists in Iran, the truth is increasingly being treated as a security threat. Authorities are tightening an already repressive reporting environment, where information is strictly controlled.

item.title: Can Argentina’s Milei use Trump ties to challenge the UK?
item.description: Argentina's Milei may use Trump ties to challenge the UK over the islands. As US-UK relations nosedive, questions are mounting over whether Trump might shift Washington's position on the islands.

item.description: Lufthansa is searching for a lost Oscar after a US airport security row. Lufthansa says searching for Oscar lost after US airport security row Tioga Publishing.
